jobs.title: Software Development Engineer, Last Mile Platform Services, SDE
jobs.exp_hint: - 3+ years of non-internship professional software deve
jobs.description:
Amazon's Last Mile Technology team brings new technology to the hardest problems in last mile delivery. We want a top-in-class experience, not only for the customer receiving a package but also for the transporters who deliver millions of them every day. Real innovation in this space is part of who we are.
How Amazon speaks to its transporters is one of the most critical systems in Last Mile. The Rabbit Communications Platform owns every surface Amazon uses to reach a Delivery Partner, Delivery Associate or Flex driver: Newsfeed, push notifications, in-app messaging, automated calls and automated customer contact. It runs on Android, iOS and wearables, worldwide. When a severe-weather shelter-in-place directive has to reach a driver in their own language, or a customer's gate code needs to travel from one delivery to the next, those journeys run on what we build. And for the driver, every one of them ends on the phone in their hand.
We are looking for talented Android and iOS Software Development Engineers to design and build the client side of these mission-critical systems. You will work on hard problems at fleet scale, on devices that are moving, often offline and running low on battery, and you will have the autonomy to deliver impactful solutions. You will develop and operate tier-1 communication surfaces in native Android (Kotlin) and iOS (Swift).
You will learn how to build server-driven, self-service client surfaces that take app releases off the critical path for communications. You'll design driver-safe interaction patterns for people who are behind the wheel or walking to a door. You'll engineer offline-first sync and message delivery across 1-to-N broadcast and 1-to-1 push. You'll internationalize and localize an app that runs in dozens of languages, including right-to-left scripts, across global markets. You'll extend these experiences to wearables. And you'll hold the crash-free rate, startup latency, battery, data-usage and accessibility standards…
